603	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
604	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
605	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
606	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
607	]
608	```
609	
610	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
611	
612	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
613	
614	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
615	
616	```json
617	{
618	  "version": "2.0",
619	  "resources": [
620	    {
621	      "resource": "Connection",
622	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	      "value": {
625	        "ConnectionId": {
626	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
627	          "isExpression": false,
628	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
629	        }
630	      },
631	      "metadata": {
632	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
633	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
634	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
635	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
636	        "Connector": "uipath-atlassian-jira"
637	      }
638	    }
639	  ]
640	}
641	```
642	
643	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
644	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
645	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
646	
647	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
648	
649	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.
650	
651	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
652	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
653	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
654	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
655	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
656	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |
657	
658	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.

662	## Debug
663	
664	### Common Errors
665	
666	| Error | Cause | Fix |
667	| --- | --- | --- |
668	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
669	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
670	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
671	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
672	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
673	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
674	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
675	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
676	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
677	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |
678	| FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when activity is reopened in Studio Web; flow runs at debug | A raw `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` string was passed instead of a structured filter tree, so `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>` is empty. The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
679	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
680	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
681	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
682	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
683	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass an array value matching the field's `dataType`, and re-run `node configure`. Fields with `[*].` (segments after the `[*]`) are not authorable. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
684	
685	### Debug Tips
686	
687	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
688	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
689	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
690	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
691	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
692	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.

1	# Run — Execute a Flow
2	
3	Execute a flow on demand and monitor progress. Three modes: **debug** (controlled re-run with full Studio Web visibility), **process run** (trigger a deployed process), **job inspection** (status and traces). All require `uip login`.
4	
5	## Pre-flight
6	
7	1. **Logged in.** `uip login status --output json` returns success. See [shared/cli-conventions.md — Login state](../../shared/cli-conventions.md#5-login-state).
8	2. **For debug runs: solution resources refreshed.** Always run before `flow debug` so connection and process resource declarations are in sync with project bindings:
9	
10	   ```bash
11	   uip solution resources refresh --solution-folder <SolutionDir> --output json
12	   ```
13	
14	## Debug — controlled end-to-end run
15	
16	> **Confirm consent first.** `flow debug` executes the flow for real — sends emails, posts messages, calls APIs. See the consent-before-debug rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md). Do not run without explicit user authorization.
17	
18	```bash
19	UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info uip maestro flow debug <path-to-project-dir> --output json
20	```
21	
22	The argument is the **project directory path** (the folder containing `project.uiproj`). Use `<ProjectName>/` from the solution dir, or `.` if already inside the project dir.
23	
24	Pass input arguments when the flow has input parameters:
25	
26	```bash
27	UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info uip maestro flow debug <path-to-project-dir> --output json \
28	  --inputs '{"numberA": 5, "numberB": 7}'
29	```
30	
31	Bind local files to file-typed input variables with `--attachment <variableId>=<localPath>` (repeatable). `<variableId>` (left of `=`) must match the `id` of a `variables.globals[]` entry with `direction:"in"` and `type:"file"`:
32	
33	```bash
34	# Replace <variableId> and <localPath> placeholders below with your own values.
35	UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info uip maestro flow debug <path-to-project-dir> --output json \
36	  --attachment <variableId>=<localPath> \
37	  --attachment <variableId>=<localPath>
38	```
39	
40	> **Pre-flight.** Confirm each `<variableId>` exists in the flow's `variables.globals[]` with `direction:"in"` and `type:"file"`. See [shared/cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](../../shared/cli-commands.md#pre-flight---attachment-binding).
41	
42	> **Reading the bound file.** At runtime a `file` variable is an object — a Script node reads the uploaded name via `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}.FullName`. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
43	
44	### Reporting debug runs to the user
45	
46	The CLI response includes a **Studio Web URL** (where the user inspects the run) and an **instanceId** (for log/trace correlation). Parse both from the JSON output — typically `Data.studioWebUrl` and `Data.instanceId` — and **always show them as the first two lines of the summary**:
47	
48	```text
49	Studio Web URL: <url>
50	Instance ID: <instanceId>
51	
52	<run status, node traces, errors, etc.>
53	```
54	
55	If either value is missing from the response, emit the label with `<not returned by CLI>` rather than dropping the line. Do not bury these values below the run summary — the user should see them immediately without scrolling.
56	
57	See [shared/cli-commands.md — uip maestro flow debug](../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-debug) for additional options.
58	
59	## Process run — trigger a deployed process
60	
61	For flows already deployed to Orchestrator (via [ship.md](ship.md) → Orchestrator path):
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow process list --output json                           # discover deployed processes
65	uip maestro flow process run <process-key> <folder-key> --output json # trigger a run
66	```
67	
68	Pass input arguments and/or bind file-typed input variables:
69	
70	```bash
71	# Replace <variableId> and <localPath> placeholders below with your own values.
72	uip maestro flow process run <process-key> <folder-key> --output json \
73	  --inputs '{"numberA": 5, "numberB": 7}' \
74	  --attachment <variableId>=<localPath>
75	```
76	
77	> **Pre-flight.** Confirm each `<variableId>` exists in the flow's `variables.globals[]` with `direction:"in"` and `type:"file"` — see [shared/cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](../../shared/cli-commands.md#pre-flight---attachment-binding). On `process run` only: `--attachment` overrides `--inputs` on key collisions; `--validate` accepts pre-uploaded attachment references for file-typed slots (passes the JSON-schema check even though the slot's nominal type is `string`).
78	
79	Run `uip maestro flow process --help` for all subcommands and options.
80	
81	## Job inspection — status and traces
82	
83	```bash
84	uip maestro flow job status <job-key> --output json   # check status of a running or completed job
85	uip maestro flow job traces <job-key> --output json   # stream the verbose execution timeline
86	```
87	
88	> **Traces are verbose** and contain the full execution timeline. Use them only when needed for diagnosis — start from incidents first via [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
89	
90	## What's next
91	
92	- **Run failed?** Triage via [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) — start with incidents, escalate to traces only if needed.
93	- **Need to intervene in a running instance** (pause, resume, cancel, retry)? See [manage.md](manage.md).
94	
95	## Anti-patterns
96	
97	- **Never run `flow debug` as a validation step.** Use `uip maestro flow validate` for correctness checking; debug is for end-to-end execution.
98	- **Never skip `solution resources refresh` before debug.** Stale resource declarations cause runtime binding failures even when the local `.flow` is correct.
99	- **Never start diagnosis from `job traces`.** Traces are last-resort — see [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) for the priority ladder.

1	# Ship — Publish a Flow
2	
3	Publish journey for a Flow project. Two paths: **Studio Web upload** (default) and **Orchestrator deploy** (only when explicitly requested). Both require `uip login`.
4	
5	> **When to use which path:** if the user says "publish" without specifying where, default to Studio Web. Only use Orchestrator deploy when the user explicitly asks to deploy to Orchestrator. Studio Web upload lets the user visualize, inspect, edit, and publish from the browser; Orchestrator deploy puts the flow directly into a process, bypassing Studio Web — the user cannot visualize or edit it there.
6	
7	## Pre-flight
8	
9	Before either publish path, ensure:
10	
11	1. **Authoring is complete.** `uip maestro flow validate` passes and `uip maestro flow format` was run. If not, send the user back to [author/CAPABILITY.md](../../author/CAPABILITY.md).
12	2. **Logged in.** `uip login status --output json` returns success. See [shared/cli-conventions.md — Login state](../../shared/cli-conventions.md#5-login-state).
13	3. **Solution resources are refreshed.** Always run this before `solution upload` or `solution publish` so that connection and process resource declarations are in sync with the project bindings:
14	
15	   ```bash
16	   uip solution resources refresh --solution-folder <SolutionDir> --output json
17	   ```
18	
19	   `<SolutionDir>` is the solution directory (containing the `.uipx` file). The command has no positional solution argument; omit `--solution-folder` only when the current directory is already the solution root.
20	
21	## Path 1 — Studio Web upload (default)
22	
23	After `solution resources refresh`, upload the solution to Studio Web:
24	
25	```bash
26	uip solution upload <SolutionDir> --output json
27	```
28	
29	`uip solution upload` accepts the solution directory directly — no intermediate bundling step required. Use the exact solution root path (or `.` from inside the solution root). If your shell is inside the nested flow project folder, pass the absolute solution root path or `..`; do not pass the solution name again, because that resolves to a child path that does not exist. If the project was created with `uip maestro flow init`, it already lives inside a solution directory. The command pushes it to Studio Web where the user can visualize, inspect, edit, and publish from the browser.
30	
31	**Share the Studio Web URL with the user** when the upload succeeds.
32	
33	## Path 2 — Orchestrator deploy (explicit only)
34	
35	Use this path **only when the user explicitly asks to deploy to Orchestrator.** Otherwise, default to Studio Web.
36	
37	Pack the flow project into a `.nupkg` then publish via the platform skill:
38	
39	```bash
40	# 1. Refresh solution resources
41	uip solution resources refresh --solution-folder <SolutionDir> --output json
42	
43	# 2. Pack
44	uip maestro flow pack <project-path> <OutputDir>
45	```
46	
47	For `uip solution publish` and the rest of the deployment workflow, see [/uipath:uipath-solution](/uipath:uipath-solution). See [shared/cli-commands.md — uip maestro flow pack](../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-pack) for `pack` flags.
48	
49	## Anti-patterns
50	
51	- **Never run `solution upload` without `solution resources refresh` first.** Stale resource declarations cause runtime binding failures (the deployed flow can't find its connections).
52	- **Never default to Orchestrator deploy when the user said "publish".** "Publish" without specifier means Studio Web. When the target is ambiguous, ask the user with **Studio Web upload** / **Orchestrator deploy** / **Something else** as options before running `flow pack` + `solution publish`. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).
53	- **Never publish a flow that hasn't been validated and formatted.** `flow validate` catches schema errors; `flow format` ensures Studio Web renders nodes correctly. Both are author-side gates — see [author/CAPABILITY.md](../../author/CAPABILITY.md).
54	
55	## What's next
56	
57	After Studio Web upload, the user typically wants to **debug** the flow end-to-end against real systems. See [run.md](run.md). After Orchestrator deploy, the user typically wants to **trigger and monitor** the deployed process — also [run.md](run.md).

21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
50	
51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
106	
107	### Instance-specific identity fields
108	
109	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
110	
111	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
112	|-------|---------|---------|
113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
114	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
115	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
117	
118	Example — manual start trigger:
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "id": "start",
123	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
124	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
125	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
126	  "inputs": {
127	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
128	  },
129	  "outputs": {
130	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "The return value of the trigger.", "source": "=result.response", "var": "output" }
131	  }
132	}
133	```
134	
135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
187	
188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
223	
224	## Edge — both ports required
225	
226	```json
227	{
228	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
229	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
230	  "sourcePort": "output",
231	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
232	  "targetPort": "input"
233	}
234	```
235	
236	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
237	>
238	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
239	
240	## Definition entry
241	
242	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
243	
244	```bash
245	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
246	```
247	
248	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
249	
250	## Common node types
251	
252	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
253	|------|---------|------------|
254	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
255	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
256	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
257	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
258	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
259	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
260	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
261	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
262	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
263	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
264	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
265	
266	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
267	
268	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
269	
270	Discover all available types:
271	```bash
272	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
273	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
274	```
275	
276	## Standard ports by node type
277	
278	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
279	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
280	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
281	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
282	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
283	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
284	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
285	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
286	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
287	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
288	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
289	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
290	
291	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
292	
293	Verify exact ports for any node type:
294	```bash
295	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
296	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
297	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
298	```
299	
300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |
349	
350	## Minimal working example — dice roller
351	
352	Building a flow is a two-step process: write the nodes/edges structure, then populate `definitions` from the registry.
353	
354	### Step 1 — Write nodes and edges
355	
356	Replace `<uuid>` with any generated UUID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` in Node.js, or any UUID v4 generator). The same UUID must appear in `entry-points.json` as `uniqueId`. Set top-level `version` to the value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds — never hand-pick it (see [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)).
357	
358	```json
359	{
360	  "id": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5",
361	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
362	  "name": "DiceRoller",
363	  "nodes": [
364	    {
365	      "id": "start",
366	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
367	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
368	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
369	      "inputs": {
370	        "entryPointId": "<uuid>"
371	      },
372	      "outputs": {
373	        "output": {
374	          "type": "object",
375	          "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
376	          "source": "=result.response",
377	          "var": "output"
378	        }
379	      }
380	    },
381	    {
382	      "id": "rollDice",
383	      "type": "core.action.script",
384	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
385	      "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
386	      "inputs": {
387	        "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
388	      },
389	      "outputs": {
390	        "output": {
391	          "type": "object",
392	          "description": "The return value of the script",
393	          "source": "=result.response",
394	          "var": "output"
395	        },
396	        "error": {
397	          "type": "object",
398	          "description": "Error information if the script fails",
399	          "source": "=result.Error",
400	          "var": "error"
401	        }
402	      }
403	    },
404	    {
405	      "id": "end",
406	      "type": "core.logic.terminate",
407	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
408	      "display": { "label": "End" },
409	      "inputs": {}
410	    }
411	  ],
412	  "edges": [
413	    {
414	      "id": "edge-start-roll",
415	      "sourceNodeId": "start",
416	      "sourcePort": "output",
417	      "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
418	      "targetPort": "input"
419	    },
420	    {
421	      "id": "edge-roll-end",
422	      "sourceNodeId": "rollDice",
423	      "sourcePort": "success",
424	      "targetNodeId": "end",
425	      "targetPort": "input"
426	    }
427	  ],
428	  "definitions": [],
429	  "bindings": [],
430	  "variables": {},
431	  "layout": {
432	    "nodes": {
433	      "start": {
434	        "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
435	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
436	        "collapsed": false
437	      },
438	      "rollDice": {
439	        "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
440	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
441	        "collapsed": false
442	      },
443	      "end": {
444	        "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
445	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
446	        "collapsed": false
447	      }
448	    }
449	  }
450	}
451	```
452	
453	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
454	
455	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
456	
457	```bash
458	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
459	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
460	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
461	```
462	
463	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
464	
465	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
466	
467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.
470	
471	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
472	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
473	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
474	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
475	
476	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
477	
478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
519	
520	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
521	
522	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
523	
524	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
525	
526	## Bindings — connector connection binding
527	
528	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
529	
530	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.

1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	When an HTTP node has an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly.
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
180	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
181	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
182	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
183	  "targetPort": "input"
184	}
185	```
186	
187	### Debug
188	
189	| Error | Cause | Fix |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
192	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
193	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
194	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
195	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
196	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
197	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
198	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |
199

1	# HTTP Request Node — Connector Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when the target service has an IS connector and you want managed auth (OAuth / API key) handled by an existing IS connection.
4	
5	**Prerequisite:** a healthy IS connection for the target connector. Step 2 verifies this. If none exists, propose manual mode as the fallback and confirm the switch with the user before finalizing — do not switch modes without that confirmation.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–5 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Steps 2 and 3 reuse it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 3 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
17	
18	## Step 2 — Identify target connection
19	
20	**Connector mode only works if the connector supports the HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<target-connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag. If the flag is false, **STOP** — a connection cannot help. Use the recovery question below (switch to manual mode / skip / something else; the create-a-connection option does not apply) and do not switch modes without confirmation.
21	
22	```bash
23	uip is connections list "<target-connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory for discovery. Selection rules, empty-result recovery, and ping verification live in the platform skill — do not duplicate them here.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md).
29	
30	Record the chosen connection's `Id` and `FolderKey` — Step 3 needs both.
31	
32	> **HTTP-specific recovery — no usable connection.** If platform-skill recovery yields nothing (empty after `--all-folders` + `--refresh`, user declines to create one), the HTTP node has unique fallback options. Ask the user to confirm the path — **manual mode is the recommended auto-fallback**, pre-selected, since it unblocks the node without a connection:
33	>
34	> - **Switch this node to manual mode** *(recommended)* — abandon this walkthrough and follow [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md). Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so this needs explicit confirmation.
35	> - **Create a new connection now** — `uip is connections create "<target-connector-key>"` starts the OAuth flow. User completes browser auth themselves, then re-run `uip is connections list` to pick up the new connection.
36	> - **Skip this node**.
37	> - **Something else**.
38	>
39	> Auto-try the fallback, but do not finalize a mode switch without the user's confirmation; do not invent a placeholder ID; do not skip the node without explicit selection. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
40	
41	## Step 3 — Configure the node
42	
43	> **STOP — open the platform skill before configuring.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, read [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md) and resolve every value you don't already have (IDs from names, required body fields, endpoint path, response shape).
44	>
45	> - **If the target connector is listed in that skill's `vendor-docs-registry.json`:** you MUST follow its **Step 0 (Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs)** — read the `docsUrl` + `notes` and confirm the exact endpoint with the `http-request` probe before running `node configure`. Pass the endpoint path verbatim: vendor method names can contain literal dots (Slack ``chat.postMessage`) — the dot is part of the path segment.
46	> - **If the connector is NOT listed:** the registry-grounding step does not apply — resolve missing values via the `http-request` probe / vendor docs as usual.
47	
48	```bash
49	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
50	  --detail '{
51	    "authentication": "connector",
52	    "targetConnector": "<target-connector-key>",
53	    "connectionId": "<target-connection-id>",
54	    "folderKey": "<folder-key>",
55	    "method": "GET",
56	    "url": "/api/endpoint",
57	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
58	  }' --output json
59	```
60	
61	> **Connector mode supports `application/json` request and response bodies only.**
62	
63	The CLI:
64	
65	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (connector, connectionId, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
66	- Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url` from the single `url` value you pass
67	- Generates `bindings_v2.json`
68	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
69	
70	**Dynamic values:** connector input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
71	
72	## Step 4 — (Optional) Response branches
73	
74	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 5 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
75	
76	## Step 5 — Wire edges
77	
78	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 4 entry). Wire `default` to the next node and `error` to a handler — without an `error` edge, a failed call faults the flow.
79	
80	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
81	
82	## Debug

slack.notes: Method-per-operation (e.g. chat.postMessage). Static schema; same for every workspace.

salesforce.notes: Per-org custom fields end in __c. Lookups via SOQL query with literal spaces.

jira.notes: Custom fields keyed customfield_*. Field set depends on project + issue type (parent fields).

servicenow.notes: Base URL already includes /api/now; Table API is versioned: /v1/table/<table>. Custom columns prefixed u_. WARNING: connector mangles = and ^ in sysparm_query (literal AND %-encoded) -> use =/^-free operators (STARTSWITH/LIKE) and refine client-side; verify the filter applied via row count. sysparm_fields/sysparm_limit honored.

mailchimp.notes: Audience (list) merge fields are per-list, keyed by tag (FNAME, LNAME, plus custom). CASCADING: the add/update-member body field set depends on list_id (a PATH param) -> author as a discovery resource (scopeFields:[list_id], path /lists/{list_id}/merge-fields?count=1000, fieldsAt:merge_fields). Discovered values go under merge_fields.<TAG>; static fields are email_address/status/email_type/vip/language).

outlook.notes: Microsoft Graph. Base https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0; mail under /me/messages, /users/{id}/messages; calendar under /me/events. OData $filter/$select/$top/$orderby. Pagination via @odata.nextLink (follow as-is). Custom mail props via singleValueExtendedProperties/openExtensionProperties (per-tenant). immutableId vs default id quirk on messages.

onedrive.notes: Microsoft Graph (OneDrive & SharePoint). Base /v1.0. Files under /me/drive, /drives/{id}/items, /sites/{id}/drive. SharePoint list custom columns surface as listItem fields (per-list, tenant-specific). @odata.nextLink pagination, OData $filter/$expand. Path addressing /items/root:/path/to/file: vs item-id. delta query for change tracking.

gmail.notes: Base https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/{userId}/... ; use 'me' for userId. Fixed schema. Pagination via pageToken/nextPageToken. messages.list filters via q= Gmail search syntax (from:, subject:, is:unread, after:). Message bodies base64url-encoded in payload.parts. Raw uploads at /upload/gmail/v1/. batchModify/batchDelete take ID arrays.

googledrive.notes: Base https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/; uploads at /upload/drive/v3/files (uploadType=media|multipart|resumable). Fixed schema. files.list pagination via pageToken/nextPageToken; filter via q= search syntax (mimeType=, name contains, 'PARENT_ID' in parents, trashed=false). Default fields sparse -> pass fields= to expand. Shared Drives need supportsAllDrives=true. Export Google-native docs via files/{id}/export.

googlesheets.notes: Base https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}. Ranges use A1 notation in path, URL-encode (e.g. Sheet1!A1:C10). values.get/update/append; valueInputOption=RAW|USER_ENTERED required on writes. Multi-range via values:batchGet?ranges=...&ranges=...; structural edits via :batchUpdate. Cell contents are arbitrary user data -> no fixed column schema.

teams.notes: Microsoft Graph. Base /v1.0. /teams/{id}/channels/{id}/messages, /chats/{id}/messages. @odata.nextLink pagination; many message/list endpoints reject arbitrary $filter (limited OData support). Fixed schema; no tenant custom fields on core objects.

openai.notes: Fixed host https://api.openai.com/v1. POST /v1/chat/completions. Auth: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. Static schema same for all callers; model selected via body "model". Streaming via SSE ("stream": true). Newer Responses API exists but chat/completions is canonical.

dynamicscrm.notes: Dataverse Web API, OData v4. Base path /api/data/v9.2/. Tenant-specific custom entities + custom columns; custom logical names carry publisher prefix (new_, cr123_), entity set pluralized in URL. $filter/$select/$expand. No $skip -> page via Prefer: odata.maxpagesize header + @odata.nextLink/$skiptoken; default cap 5000 rows. Lookups set via @odata.bind. Auth: Azure AD OAuth2, resource = org URL.

datadog.notes: Site-specific host: api.datadoghq.com (US1), api.us3/us5.datadoghq.com, api.datadoghq.eu (EU1), api.ap1/ap2.datadoghq.com, api.ddog-gov.com. Wrong site 403s. Auth headers: DD-API-KEY (all), DD-APPLICATION-KEY (most read/scoped endpoints). Versioned paths /api/v1 and /api/v2 coexist. Pagination via page[cursor]/cursor params on v2.

netsuite.notes: SuiteTalk REST. Base https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/rest. Records at /record/v1/<recordType>; SuiteQL at /query/v1/suiteql (POST, body {"q":...}, set Prefer: transient). Per-account custom fields prefixed custentity_/custbody_; custom record types custrecord_/customrecord_. Pagination limit/offset query params (max 1000/page), next via links. Auth: OAuth2 or token-based (TBA). Record schemas at system.netsuite.com REST_API_Browser.

snowflake.notes: Account-specific host https://<account_identifier>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2. POST /statements to run SQL; returns 202 + statementHandle if not finished -> poll GET /statements/{handle} until 200; cancel via POST /statements/{handle}/cancel. Async via ?async=true. Auth: Bearer JWT(key-pair)/OAuth. Large results partitioned. Tables/columns are tenant-defined -> schema not inferable from docs.

github.notes: Base https://api.github.com. Set Accept: application/vnd.github+json and X-GitHub-Api-Version (default 2022-11-28). Pagination via Link header (rel=next/last) + per_page/page query params, NOT OData. No $filter; resource-specific query params. Fixed schema.

workday.notes: Tenant-specific base host: https://{host}.workday.com/ccx/api/{service}/{version}/{tenant}/{endpoint} (e.g. .../api/wql/v1/{tenant}/data). Per-service versioning (workers v6, common v1, wql v1). WQL endpoint runs read-only queries; RaaS exposes custom reports. Pagination: limit (max 100) + offset. Auth: OAuth2 bearer, API client scoped per service. Custom fields/objects + report data sources are tenant-defined -> discover via tenant API explorer, not generic docs.

azure.notes: Azure Resource Manager REST. Base host https://management.azure.com. Every request requires ?api-version=YYYY-MM-DD (per-resource-provider; omitting it 400s). Auth: Bearer OAuth2 (AAD, scope https://management.azure.com/.default). Paginate via nextLink in response body. Fixed schema per resource provider.

azuread.notes: Microsoft Graph. Base https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0 (use v1.0, not beta, for prod). Auth: Bearer OAuth2 (scope https://graph.microsoft.com/.default). Paginate via @odata.nextLink. Directory extension attributes + open/schema extensions are tenant-specific custom fields not in docs; query with $select. Advanced filters need ConsistencyLevel:eventual header + $count.

aws.notes: No single REST API; per-service endpoints host https://<service>.<region>.amazonaws.com (e.g. ec2.us-east-1.amazonaws.com). All requests require SigV4 signing (canonical request + Authorization header scoped to service+region+date; clock skew >5min rejected). Many services are query/JSON-RPC, not pure REST. Pagination via NextToken/marker per service. SigV4 ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html

box.notes: Box Content API. Base https://api.box.com/2.0; uploads use https://upload.box.com/api/2.0. Marker-based pagination: marker + limit query params, next_marker in response (null = done); some endpoints offset-based, force marker with usemarker=true. Custom fields live in tenant-defined metadata templates (scope enterprise_<id>, templateKey); query via POST /metadata_queries/execute_read. Auth: OAuth2.

sapodata.notes: SAP S/4HANA + C4C OData v2 (not v4). Service path /sap/opc/odata/sap/<SERVICE>/ varies by tenant-activated service. Tenant custom OData services + Z-fields/custom entities not in standard docs. $filter (OData v2 operators eq/ne/gt/substringof), $select/$expand/$orderby; pagination $top/$skip + $inlinecount=allpages or __next link. CSRF: GET with X-CSRF-Token: Fetch before writes. Auth: Basic or OAuth2.

vertex.notes: Regional host {LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com (e.g. us-central1-); 'global' uses aiplatform.googleapis.com. Versions v1 (stable) / v1beta1. Generative: POST projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/{model}:generateContent (streamGenerateContent for streaming). Custom endpoints: endpoints/{id}:predict. countTokens/computeTokens separate. Body schema fixed per model.

agentforce.notes: Host https://api.salesforce.com (gov: api.gov.salesforce.com). Flow: start session (needs per-org AGENT_ID), POST message to session, end session. Auth: OAuth client-credentials via external client app (consumer key/secret + my-domain) -> Bearer token. AGENT_ID and Flows are per-org -> not knowable from docs.

databricks.notes: Workspace-specific host https://<workspace-host>/serving-endpoints/{name}/invocations (POST). Endpoint {name} (agent/model) is workspace-defined -> not knowable from docs. Auth: Bearer PAT/OAuth. Body shape depends on endpoint type: chat/completions/embeddings for foundation/external models (extra_params), dataframe_records/dataframe_split for custom models.

snowflakecortex.notes: Account-specific host https://<account_identifier>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/cortex. OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions (also Anthropic-style /v1/messages). Auth: Bearer JWT/OAuth/PAT. Streaming via SSE ("stream": true). Model availability region-gated; host is per-account.

powerautomate.notes: Power Platform API. Base https://api.powerplatform.com/{namespace}/{resource}; mandatory api-version query param (e.g. 2024-10-01). Environment-scoped resources need environmentId in path; tenant inferred from bearer token. Flows stored in Dataverse (Workflow table) -> alt access via Dataverse Web API.
